items.risk: Cross-tenant IDOR cluster in ai.rs equipment endpoints: update_equipment (ai.rs:1113), delete_equipment (ai.rs:1131), and update_maintenance (ai.rs:1192) all bind `_principal: RequestPrincipal` and discard it, then call equipment_repo.update/delete/update_maintenance with only the Path id — no tenant scoping. An authenticated user in any org can DELETE FROM equipment WHERE id=$1 / mutate any other org's equipment + maintenance rows. List/predictions siblings DO call require_tenant_id, confirming the omission is a bug not a design choice.
items.mitigation: Thread the principal's tenant_id into equipment_repo.update/delete/update_maintenance and add `AND tenant_id = $tenant` to the WHERE clauses (or use the RLS connection so the policy enforces scope). Add a cross-tenant regression test asserting 404/forbidden for foreign ids.

items.risk: Epic 6 announcement web UI (viewing/ack 6-2, comments 6-3, pin 6-4) is split across three draft PRs (#474/#475/#479) that have not merged. Backend + notification pipeline (PR #463) and WebSocket sync (PR #472) are now live, so the only thing gating story closure is the web UI landing — but a stalled three-PR draft cluster is a review-queue risk that can leave 6-2/6-3/6-4 stuck at partial.
items.mitigation: Sequence the three drafts (#474 viewing → #475 comments → #479 pin) so they merge in dependency order without conflicting on the shared AnnouncementsPage; promote out of draft once apiStatus wiring is verified.

items.risk: Post-merge review opened follow-up issues #480-#487 covering test gaps + minor security/UX follow-ups on the heavy frontend delivery (messaging realtime, document share-flow, OAuth UI, MFA). Same risk surface as the integrations/organizations/documents.rs split already actioned.
items.mitigation: Add ai.rs/platform_admin.rs/announcements.rs to the module-split backlog; add a CI grep/clippy lint that flags handlers binding `_principal` (discarded principal) on mutating routes.

items.risk: FaultStatusCount / FaultByStatusTable surfaced by the new Support Data admin page (#635) defines a fault-by-status metric for support staff. The same fault counting also exists in owner_analytics.rs and portfolio_performance.rs. If the status buckets / counting window are re-derived per route rather than from one shared definition, support, owner, and portfolio dashboards will show divergent fault numbers — eroding trust in the analytics and complicating support triage.
items.mitigation: Factor the fault-status bucket + window definition into one shared query/helper reused by the support-data, owner-analytics, and portfolio routes; add a test asserting the three surfaces return identical counts for a fixed fixture.

items.risk: The Support Data page (#635) lets support/admin staff read cross-tenant user diagnostics (memberships, sessions with IP, activity log) gated only by the audit_read capability. There is no analytics/audit event recording WHO viewed a given tenant's support data or revoked sessions — so cross-tenant PII access by support staff is not independently traceable, a privacy/retention exposure as the UI makes this access routine.
items.mitigation: Emit a support_data_viewed / support_sessions_revoked audit event (admin_user_id + target tenant/user) on each support-data read and session-revoke; bound retention on the session/activity diagnostics surfaced through the page.
